Load the **`horizon`** skill FIRST. Read it at the ABSOLUTE path
`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` (also exported as `$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`) — do NOT use a
relative path like `.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md`, which fails when your
shell starts in a member project rather than the workspace root. The skill
explains where the state lives, the tools, and this workspace's conventions
(one-shot discipline, git commits, the final report).

Before modifying files, inspect the required and conversational inbox lanes:
`"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json`
then `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json`.
Protections are standing constraints even when already read. Address or explicitly
acknowledge unread conversations before ordinary advisory inbox material.

# Task
Task: pic-d
Title: Pic rep lane D: close Pic representability, no new hypotheses
Project(s) — work across all of them:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild
References: roadmap=AJCR.jacobian,AJCR.w4-rep; inbox=I-0838

Pic representability should close, and closing it is your objective — pick a roadmap item and make major progress on it, USING NO ADDITIONAL HYPOTHESIS (`rep` has 93 consumers and 0 producers; last round added 71 more consumers and the headline did not move). Your work must be directly usable by Pic representability and the other items, not local to your row. Be ambitious: don't scope down because something is large or missing from mathlib — building substrate and huge refactoring are licensed. Delete unfaithful roadmap items and create truer ones, but never a row another lane owns at HEAD. Collaborate with the other lanes; announce what you take before you start.

YOUR PEERS this round are pic-a, pic-b, pic-c, pic-d, pic-e, pic-f, pic-g, pic-h — eight provers, no reviewer. Four work Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge (pic-a, pic-b, pic-e, pic-f) and four work Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild (pic-c, pic-d, pic-g, pic-h). With eight lanes on one ledger, announcing what you take BEFORE you start is what stops two lanes proving the same lemma — read the inbox for what the others announced, and say so if you are taking something already held.

This is a headless, one-shot session: advance the REAL objective, commit each
verified unit and any final edits, keep operational comments to the delta,
then write the skill's brief final report.

---
name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute

and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.

## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).

Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:

- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.

- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
  as **memory**.

Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

## Resuming after an interruption

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.

## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)

There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
`subagents` skill):

- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

They include two board comments I created minutes ago, five AJC inbox items, and seven comment files across four other lanes' threads.\n\nAND THE MECHANISM THIS ITEM STILL DID NOT COVER, now filed as I-1271 and independently reproduced by ajc-p2 as I-1288: THE FRESH-INDEX DISCIPLINE BELOW IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. `read-tree HEAD` snapshots the WHOLE tree; `commit` writes the WHOLE index as a tree, not only the paths you added. So any path another lane advances between your read-tree and your commit is silently REVERTED by your commit -- as an M against a stale blob, with no D line, and with every pre-commit check passing because HEAD had not moved when you ran them. It happened to me this session on ajc-p1's galois row (3bf50581e7), restored byte-identical in 83abf6dc00.\n\nSO THE COMPLETE PROCEDURE, both halves required:\n 1. BEFORE: fresh index file (rm -f), read-tree HEAD, add ONLY explicit paths, confirm the staged stat lists only those paths, commit -- all with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at that file. Never copy the shared index; never read-tree HEAD into it (I-0999).\n 2. AFTER, and this is the half that catches the race: `diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat` and READ EVERY PATH. A path you did not add means you reverted it; restore from disk, which still holds their version. Also read the DELETION COUNT rather than the exit code.\nI ran step 2 on all ten of my commits this session; it caught the one clobber within a minute.\n\n--- earlier r6 box and the original r5 body follow; their seven- and twenty-three-path lists are both superseded ---\n\nAUTHOR RE-MEASUREMENT r6: MY HEADLINE NUMBER IS STALE AND THE FAILURE MODE HAS CHANGED. So the headline below is stale about those files. They are MODIFICATIONS to stale blobs, which produce NO D line. Never copy the shared index; never read-tree HEAD into it (I-0999). AND READ THE DELETION COUNT, not the exit code -- a large deletion count in a session where you only added lines is the signal, D lines or not.\n\nI held this for my one commit this session (7acca236a0): three paths staged, stat listed exactly those three, `diff HEAD~1 HEAD` after committing showed only them.\n\nNOTHING IS LOST as of this writing: all four Lean files, my board comment and all twelve inbox items are intact at HEAD and on disk. Still a warning about the next plain commit, not a damage report.\n\nI support ajcr-p4's suggestion that the fresh-index sequence become a HUMAN-ISSUED protection rather than a lesson each lane rediscovers after clobbering someone -- three of my own r4 commits clobbered other lanes before I learned it.\n\n--- the original r5 body follows; its seven-path list is superseded above ---\n\nLIVE HAZARD: THE SHARED GIT INDEX HAS SEVEN STAGED DELETIONS OF FILES THAT EXIST AT HEAD AND ON DISK -- including EVERY new AJCR proof from this round. Do NOT commit from the shared index. Confirms and extends ajcr-p1's I-1220, whose list was shorter.\n\nRE-MEASURED by review-ajcr r5, independently. All seven verified present BOTH at HEAD and on disk:\n\n D DivisorFamilyAffClassDegree.lean   (hdegAff DISCHARGED -- p1, this round)\n D Pic0AtlasFromDivRepAff.lean        (the WIDENED Sigma-chart -- p1, this round)\n D Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean            (the V=bot refutation -- p4, this round)\n D Pic0ChartLocusH0One.lean           (p2's locus work, this round)\n D roadmap items .../c9-chartlocus.chart-u-aff.yaml  (p3's new row)\n D roadmap comments AJCR.w4-rep/C-0011.md            (my re-ranking)\n D roadmap comments .../abel-widened/C-0003.md       (my repricing)\n\nSo a plain commit from the shared index by any lane deletes this entire round's AJCR output, and it will look normal: the staged diff does show the D lines, but nobody reads a 7-line stat expecting them, and every per-file lake env lean and hash-vs-disk check PASSES, because the files themselves are fine. The damage is in the index, not the tree.\n\nWHAT TO DO INSTEAD -- the discipline that held all session for me (five commits, zero clobbering): make a FRESH index file, seed it from HEAD, add only your explicit paths, confirm the staged stat lists ONLY those paths, then commit -- all four steps with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at that fresh file. After committing, show the commit at zero context for each of your paths and confirm every added line is yours.       "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. 98 /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon-start/SKILL.md
---
name: horizon-start
description: Work out which situation you were launched into — first round of a fresh run, a hand-off from the horizon session that just finished, a resume after a crash or pause, or a session outside any run — and pull exactly the context that situation calls for. Load at the START of a session, before picking up the task.
---

Your prompt carries the task and nothing else: no history, no word about who ran
before you or how they ended. That is deliberate — state is pulled, not pushed
(the `horizon` skill's stance). But it means a session that starts working
immediately is guessing. Usually somebody *was* here before you, often minutes
ago, and their report was written for you.

This skill is the first pass: four cheap reads, a guess at the situation, then
the context that situation actually calls for. Budget a couple of minutes, not a
tenth of the session.

## The four signals

```bash
ls "$ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR/.."     # sibling sessions in THIS run
"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json             # `paused` (why the last run stopped) + `recent_failure_reasons`
"$HORIZON_BIN" ps                       # is another run live on this workspace RIGHT NOW?
"$HORIZON_GIT" log --oneline -15        # what actually landed recently
```

The sibling listing is the one that decides most of it. A run's sessions look
like:

```
0001-system            ← orchestrator bookkeeping (commits, integration), not an agent
0002-horizon-PET.5     ← a horizon session; meta.json + transcript.jsonl + usage.json
0003-system
0004-horizon-PET.5     ← ...you, probably
```

For any earlier `*-horizon-*` sibling, two files answer everything:

- **`report.md` present** → that session finished on its own terms and wrote you
  a hand-off. **`report.md` absent** → it was killed mid-flight. This is the
  single most informative bit on disk.
- **`meta.json`** → `round`, `task_id`, `status`, `started_at`, `ended_at`,
  `model`. `ended_at` against the current time tells you whether "recent" means
  four minutes ago or last week.

## Which situation am I in?

Work down the list; the first match is your best guess.

**An earlier horizon sibling has no `report.md`** → *resume after a crash or
kill.* Its work is half-done and possibly half-committed. Read its commits in
the ledger first (they are the part that survived), then the tail of its
transcript to see what it was in the middle of — `usage --json` `paused` gives
the reason it died (usage limit, budget, auth), and `recent_failure_reasons`
shows rate-limit pressure that may still be there. Trust the ledger over the
transcript: anything it did not commit is gone, no matter what it said it was
doing. If the dead session shares your `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK`, you are continuing
its exact work — pick up its front rather than opening a new one.

**An earlier horizon sibling has a `report.md`** → *hand-off from the session
that just finished.* The common case. Read that report first — its `## Next` and
`## Why I stopped` were written for exactly this moment — then its commits, then
any inbox items addressed to horizon since its `ended_at`. Do not re-derive what
it already established; do not redo a piece it says is done without checking the
ledger.

**`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is `0` and no horizon sibling exists** → *first agent
of the run.* Nobody handed you anything **in this run** — but the workspace is
almost never greenfield. Earlier runs live under `.archon-horizon/runs/`; the
roadmap, the inbox and the ledger carry their conclusions. Skim the roadmap and
recent ledger history before deciding a strategy that a previous run already
tried and rejected.

**`ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` is unset** → *not launched by the orchestrator* (an
interactive or hand-driven session). No run context exists to reconstruct;
orient from workspace state — roadmap, inbox, ledger — and say where things
stand before proposing work.

One caveat about round numbers. `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is 0-based and reliable
for "am I first" — but a resumed run can re-run a round whose session died, so a
`0` with a dead sibling present means *resume*, not *fresh*. The dead-sibling
check settles it either way. (`ROUND + 1 == ROUNDS` is a sound last-round test,
resumed runs included — `ROUNDS` bounds the rounds *this* invocation drives, not
the run's original plan.)

## Then, before you start

- **`horizon ps` said another run is live?** You share one ledger branch with it.
  Commit in small coherent pieces and expect to see its commits interleaved.
- **Timestamps are context.** A predecessor that ended 90 seconds ago probably
  left a warm build; one that ended last week may have left a workspace that no
  longer compiles. Check rather than assume.
- **The inbox is the cross-session thread** — read what past sessions left for
  horizon, and the task's own comments if you share their `task_id`
  (`"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`). Skill:
  `horizon-inbox`.

Then stop orienting and start working. The point of this pass is to begin from a
smarter place than round zero — not to reconstruct everything that ever happened
here.

name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
  is *not* done.
- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
  for final validation.
- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.

## When the LSP dies on big import files

The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
proof error:

- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
  the specific module you are proving in instead.
- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

   476	`false`, `t₁ᵃ` on `true`.  The `Bool`-indexed form of `relFiberCoordPow` /
   477	`relFiberCoordOnePow`, which the widened sections need for the same reason
   478	`relThetaResSide` was needed for the twisting unit. -/
   479	noncomputable def relFiberCoordSidePow (n : ℕ) : ∀ b : Bool,
   480	    Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)
   481	  | false => relFiberCoordPow C R π n
   482	  | true => relFiberCoordOnePow C R π n

   485	lemma relFiberCoordSidePow_false (n : ℕ) :

   491	    relFiberCoordSidePow (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) n true

   494	/-- **The widened manufactured section at side `b`**: on each piece, the coordinate power of
   495	its *assigned* side when that side is `b`, and `1` otherwise.
   496	
   497	At `b = false` this is `thetaSectionFst` and at `b = true` it is `thetaSectionSnd`, with the
   498	`Sum`-match replaced by a `Bool` comparison against `τ.side j`. -/

   500	  if h : τ.side j = b then

   503	        (h ▸ relFiberCoordSidePow (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) a (τ.side j)))

   510	          ((relCurve C R).resHom (piece_le_relPinnedChart τ j)
   511	            (h ▸ relFiberCoordSidePow (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) a (τ.side j))) :=

   584	discipline it owes **two** probes.  "Not silently stronger" is discharged by
   585	`thetaSpan_mul_thetaInvSpan_le_one`: the automatic half is landed, so the content is exactly
   586	the reverse inclusion, the same content as chart-typed.
   587	
   588	The mirror risk is **unsatisfiability** — a `Prop` no widened cover can ever satisfy would make
   589	every consumer of it a vacuous theorem, which passes every `sorry` census and axiom probe.  The
   590	probe below rules that out with an unconditional witness, so the residue is genuinely open
   591	rather than false. -/
   592	
   593	/-- **THE SATISFIABILITY PROBE, DISCHARGED at the trivial twist.**  At `a = 0` the theta
   594	cocycle is `1`, so every `thetaOvlUnit` is `1`, both spans are the equalizer algebra itself, and
   595	the pairing holds **unconditionally** — for every widened cover, every adaptation and every
   596	chart typing.
   597	
   598	This does not make the pairing easy at `a > 0`: the content there is the manufactured sections,
   599	which is the open obligation. What it establishes is that `IsThetaPaired` is *satisfiable*, i.e.
   600	that the widened statement is not a reduction to a false hypothesis. -/
   601	theorem isThetaPaired_zero : IsThetaPaired A τ 0 := by
   602	  refine isThetaPaired_of_one_mem A τ 0 ?_
   603	  -- at the trivial twist both spans contain `1`
   604	  have hone : (1 : A.chartProd) ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A (thetaOvlUnit τ 0) := by
   605	    rw [mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff]
   606	    intro p
   607	    rw [thetaOvlUnit_zero τ p.1 p.2]
   608	    rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, map_one, map_one, Units.val_one, map_one, mul_one]
   609	  have hinvunit : (thetaOvlUnit τ 0)⁻¹
   610	      = (thetaOvlUnit τ 0 : ∀ i j : D.index,
   611	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)ˣ) := by
   612	    funext i j
   613	    rw [Pi.inv_apply, Pi.inv_apply, thetaOvlUnit_zero τ i j, inv_one]
   614	  have hinv : (1 : A.chartProd) ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A (thetaOvlUnit τ 0)⁻¹ := by
   615	    rw [hinvunit]; exact hone
   616	  have := Submodule.mul_mem_mul (mem_thetaSpan_iff A τ 0 |>.mpr hone)
   617	    (mem_thetaInvSpan_iff A τ 0 |>.mpr hinv)
   618	  rwa [one_mul] at this
   619	
   620	end Pairing

   661	    (hy₁ : y ∉ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))) :

   914	noncomputable def windowQuotEquiv (hsurj : Function.Surjective (thetaGluedEval A τ a)) :

   917	  (Submodule.quotEquivOfEq _ _ (ker_windowCarve A τ a hH1).symm).trans
   918	    ((windowCarve A τ a hH1).quotKerEquivOfSurjective
   919	      (windowCarve_surjective A τ a hH1 hsurj))
   920	
   921	end WindowCarve
   922

    11	/-!
    12	# Intrinsic theta restrictions on widened divisor-family pieces
    13	
    14	The widened cover of `AffAdaptation` consists of arbitrary affine opens.  It therefore
    15	cannot use a pinned-chart trivialization of the theta cocycle.  Instead, on each piece
    16	`D.pieces j` we choose the affine sections model of the intrinsic cocycle-glued theta
    17	line bundle `(thetaChartDatum C R π a).sheaf`.  Its sections are an invertible module
    18	over the piece ring.
    19	
    20	Base change along the quotient
    21	`Gamma(D.pieces j) -> A.colength j = Gamma(D.pieces j) / (A.eqn j)` gives the intrinsic
    22	restriction of the theta line bundle to the piece of the finite divisor.  Invertibility
    23	is preserved by this base change.  A widened certificate then makes the colength algebra
    24	finite projective over `R`, so the existing invertible-module transfer gives finite and
    25	projective `R`-modules without any chart typing or additional hypothesis.
    26	-/
    27	
    28	set_option autoImplicit false
    29	
    30	universe u
    31	
    32	open CategoryTheory Opposite TopologicalSpace
    33	open scoped TensorProduct
    34	
    35	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    36	
    37	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    38	
    39	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    40	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    41	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
    42	variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    43	
    44	namespace AffAdaptation
    45	
    46	/-- The intrinsic theta sections on the widened affine piece `j`. -/
    47	noncomputable abbrev ThetaPieceSections (_A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
    48	    (j : D.index) : Type u :=
    49	  (thetaChartDatum C R π a).sheaf.obj.obj (op (D.pieces j))
    50	
    51	/-- A canonical choice of the finite projective invertible sections model of the
    52	intrinsic theta line bundle on the widened affine piece `j`.  The choice internally
    53	refines the arbitrary piece by basic opens subordinate to the theta cover; it does not
    54	type the piece itself into either pinned chart. -/
    55	noncomputable def thetaPieceSectionsModel (_A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) (j : D.index) :
    56	    (thetaChartDatum C R π a).AffineSectionsModel (D.pieces j) :=
    57	  Classical.choice ((thetaChartDatum C R π a).nonempty_affineSectionsModel
    58	    (D.pieces j) (D.isAffineOpen j))
    59	
    60	/-- The piece-ring action on intrinsic theta sections selected by
    61	`thetaPieceSectionsModel`. -/
    62	@[reducible]
    63	noncomputable def thetaPieceSectionsModule (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) (j : D.index) :
    64	    Module Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) (A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j) :=
    65	  letI : Scheme.QcohOn (thetaChartDatum C R π a).sheaf (D.pieces j) :=
    66	    (A.thetaPieceSectionsModel (π := π) a j).qcoh
    67	  Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := (thetaChartDatum C R π a).sheaf)
    68	    (le_refl (D.pieces j))
    69	
    70	/-- The intrinsic restriction of `O(a Theta)` to the divisor inside the widened piece
    71	`j`: tensor theta sections with the equation quotient `A.colength j`. -/
    72	noncomputable abbrev ThetaPieceRestriction (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
    73	    (j : D.index) : Type u :=
    74	  letI : Module Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) (A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j) :=
    75	    A.thetaPieceSectionsModule (π := π) a j
    76	  A.colength j ⊗[Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)] A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j
    77	
    78	/-- The intrinsic theta restriction is invertible over the piece-local colength algebra.
    79	This is base-change stability of invertible modules. -/
    80	theorem invertible_thetaPieceRestriction (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) (j : D.index) :
    81	    Module.Invertible (A.colength j) (A.ThetaPieceRestriction (π := π) a j) := by
    82	  let M := A.thetaPieceSectionsModel (π := π) a j
    83	  letI : Scheme.QcohOn (thetaChartDatum C R π a).sheaf (D.pieces j) := M.qcoh
    84	  letI : Module Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) (A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j) :=
    85	    A.thetaPieceSectionsModule (π := π) a j
    86	  haveI : Module.Invertible Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)
    87	      (A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j) := M.invertible
    88	  change Module.Invertible (A.colength j)
    89	    (A.colength j ⊗[Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)]
    90	      A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j)
    91	  infer_instance
    92	
    93	/-- Under the existing widened certificate, every intrinsic theta restriction is finite
    94	over the test ring. -/
    95	theorem IsCertified.finite_thetaPieceRestriction (A : AffAdaptation D d) {n : ℕ}
    96	    (hc : A.IsCertified n) (a : ℕ) (j : D.index) :
    97	    Module.Finite R (A.ThetaPieceRestriction (π := π) a j) := by
    98	  letI : Module Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) (A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j) :=
    99	    A.thetaPieceSectionsModule (π := π) a j
   100	  haveI : Module.Invertible (A.colength j)
   101	      (A.ThetaPieceRestriction (π := π) a j) :=
   102	    A.invertible_thetaPieceRestriction (π := π) a j
   103	  haveI : Module.Finite R (A.colength j) := hc.finite_colength j
   104	  exact Module.Invertible.finite_trans (A := A.colength j)
   105	
   106	/-- Under the existing widened certificate, every intrinsic theta restriction is
   107	projective over the test ring. -/
   108	theorem IsCertified.projective_thetaPieceRestriction (A : AffAdaptation D d) {n : ℕ}
   109	    (hc : A.IsCertified n) (a : ℕ) (j : D.index) :
   110	    Module.Projective R (A.ThetaPieceRestriction (π := π) a j) := by
   111	  letI : Module Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) (A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j) :=
   112	    A.thetaPieceSectionsModule (π := π) a j
   113	  haveI : Module.Invertible (A.colength j)
   114	      (A.ThetaPieceRestriction (π := π) a j) :=
   115	    A.invertible_thetaPieceRestriction (π := π) a j
   116	  haveI : Module.Projective R (A.colength j) := hc.projective_colength j
   117	  exact Module.Invertible.projective_trans (A := A.colength j)
   118	
   119	end AffAdaptation
   120	
   121	end AlgebraicGeometry

    12	/-!
    13	# The Θ-LAYER OVER A CHART-TYPED WIDENED COVER: a real absence, on an index that R2 empties
    14	
    15	> **READ `isEmpty_chartTyping_of_straddling` (below) BEFORE THIS DOCSTRING'S ARGUMENT.**
    16	> This module's original headline was "the widened carrier had no Θ-layer, and supplying it lets
    17	> cert-r2's producer reach U2". **The first clause is true; the second is refuted, in Lean, in
    18	> this file.** Every declaration here is indexed by a `ChartTyping C R π D`, and a cover with a
    19	> straddling piece admits *none* — which is exactly the case protection `I-0492`'s widening
    20	> exists to handle. So on those divisors every theorem below is vacuous, and the tree's only
    21	> `ChartTyping` producer is the migration *from* the old chart-typed carrier. Refutation and its
    22	> consequences: `isEmpty_chartTyping_of_straddling`; reviewer items `I-0779`/`I-0782`.
    23	>
    24	> What survives is worth keeping and is not the headline: the Θ-layer genuinely did not exist on
    25	> `AffAdaptation` (measurements below, independently confirmed as `I-0780`), it ports cleanly, and
    26	> it is now available for any cover that *does* carry a chart typing.
    27	
    28	Protection `I-0492` widened the certificate carrier to arbitrary affine opens, and the
    29	widened lane now produces a class from geometry
    30	(`ThetaGeneratorSeed.divFamZarAff_of_swallowing_affineOpen`,
    31	`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffSeedGate.lean`).  That producer still cannot feed U2, and the
    32	reason recorded across five sessions — "U2 needs a certificate" — is **not** it.  The
    33	argument below correctly identifies the *absence*; where it overreaches is in treating
    34	supplying that absence as sufficient.
    35	
    36	## The measurement that renames the seam
    37	
    38	U2's consumer `DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause` (`Picard/DivRepAffPullClause.lean:121`)
    39	quantifies over `DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) π g`, the *chart-typed* value.  There is no
    40	map `DivFamZarAff → DivFamZar` and there cannot be (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 §2:
    41	a straddling divisor has no chart-typed certificate).  So the only usable route is to
    42	re-derive the ε-value facts on the widened carrier — and *that* is where the absence is:
    43	
    44	> `divFamEps_eq_of_le` (`Picard/DivRepChartClassUnivQuot.lean`) needs projectivity and
    45	> constant rank `g` of the **window quotient**.  On `DivFam` those are landed
    46	> *unconditionally* (`Picard/DivSchemeFrameCover.lean:106`/`:117`) — but their only proof
    47	> route is `windowQuotEquiv` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyWindow.lean:179`), whose target is
    48	> `A.ThetaGlued a`, and `ThetaGlued` / `thetaGluedEval` / `thetaOvlUnit` /
    49	> `thetaDeltaRight` / `ker_thetaGluedEval` are defined **only** on `DivisorAdaptation`
    50	> (`Picard/DivisorFamilyTheta.lean`).
    51	
    52	Cross-measured at HEAD: of the files mentioning `AffAdaptation`, **zero** define any theta
    53	arrow.  `DivisorFamilyAffFraming.lean` is right that the ε-pair *statement* is
    54	carrier-indifferent (both carriers have the same `eqns` field and `divisorWindow` reads
    55	nothing else); the ε-pair **facts** are not, and statement was never separated from facts.
    56	
    57	## Why this is a port and not new mathematics
    58	
    59	The Θ-layer's chart-dependence is exactly **one `Bool` per piece**.  `FinCoverData`'s
    60	version reads it off the `Sum` index (`pieces_inl_le` / `pieces_inr_le`), which is why it
    61	looks chart-typed; but the side-uniform API it could have used already exists and is
    62	consumed by some sixty files:
    63	
    64	* `relThetaResSide` (`Picard/DivSchemeFamilySide.lean:155`) — the side component,
    65	  restricted into any open below `relPinnedChart (side j)`;
    66	* `relThetaSideUnit` (`:180`) — the matching unit of an ordered pair of sides, whose
    67	  four-case split *is* `FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit`'s;
    68	* `relThetaResSide_matching` (`:194`) and `resHom_relThetaResSide` (`:172`).
    69	
    70	Each needs only `piece ≤ relPinnedChart (side j)` — which is **verbatim** the field
    71	`ChartTyping.piece_le` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean:204`), the datum `I-0492`
    72	clause 3 deliberately kept *separate* from the certificate clauses precisely so the
    73	Θ-layer could have it without the certificate demanding it.
    74	
    75	So this file is the missing face, built the way clause 3 intends: the twisting data is
    76	indexed by a `ChartTyping`, and **no certificate clause and no locally-certified predicate
    77	mentions it**.
    78	
    79	## What this file does and does not claim
    80	
    81	It builds the widened Θ-twisted glued module and its evaluation, and proves the kernel
    82	bridge — left exactness, i.e. that the kernel is the *same* cover-independent vanishing
    83	submodule the chart-typed layer produces.  That is the input `windowQuotEquiv`'s widened
    84	analogue needs.
    85	
    86	It does **not** prove surjectivity of the widened evaluation (the right-exactness heart,
    87	`thetaGluedEval_surjective`'s analogue), and it does not produce a widened ε-value
    88	identity: those consume the widened certificate's (c2) clause through a widened
    89	`IsThetaPaired`, which is the next face and is *not* built here.  Read this as "the
    90	ε-value facts are now *stateable* over the widened carrier", not as a gate cleared.
    91	
    92	## Main declarations
    93	
    94	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation.thetaOvlUnit` — the twisting unit of an ordered pair of
    95	  widened pieces, read off a `ChartTyping` rather than a `Sum` index.
    96	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation.thetaGluedSubmodule` / `ThetaGlued` — the Θ-twisted
    97	  glued colength module over a widened cover, spelled as a kernel exactly as the
    98	  chart-typed one.
    99	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation.thetaGluedEval` — the evaluation
   100	  `H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ)) → W(d)^{Θᵃ}`.
   101	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation.ker_thetaGluedEval` — **the kernel bridge**: the widened
   102	  kernel *is* the cover-independent vanishing submodule, hence literally the chart-typed
   103	  layer's kernel.
   104	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation.windowCarve` / `ker_windowCarve` / `windowQuotEquiv` — the
   105	  bridge plugged in: the widened carve arrow's kernel is `divisorWindow d`, and (conditional on
   106	  surjectivity, which is **not** proved here) the quotient of the free window by it is the
   107	  widened `W(d)^{Θᵃ}`.  That last equivalence is the vehicle whose absence made the ε-value at a
   108	  `DivFamZarAff` unstateable.
   109	
   110	**A phrasing correction taken from a fresh-context review** (`I-0769`), because the wrong version
   111	was in this docstring: `ker_thetaGluedEval` does **not** show "`divisorWindow` is the same on both
   112	carriers" — `divisorWindow` takes only `d` and `hH1` and never mentioned a carrier, so that is
   113	vacuous.  The content runs the other way: *the widened evaluation's kernel lands on that
   114	already-fixed submodule.*
   115	-/
   116	
   117	set_option autoImplicit false
   118	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
   119	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161), so the pinned synthesis
   120	depth must be set in-file for the faithful per-file check. -/
   121	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
   122	
   123	universe u
   124	
   125	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
   126	open scoped TensorProduct
   127	
   128	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   129	
   130	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
   131	
   132	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   133	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
   134	/- `ChartTyping` is stated with an `[IsAffineHom π]` binder, which `[IsFinite π]` already
   135	supplies — the `overlappingInstances` linter reports the pair, so only `IsFinite` is taken
   136	here and `IsAffineHom` is found by synthesis. -/
   137	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
   138	
   139	namespace AffAdaptation
   140	
   141	variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
   142	variable (A : AffAdaptation D d) (τ : ChartTyping C R π D) (a : ℕ)
   143	
   144	/-! ## The twisting unit, read off a chart typing
   145	
   146	`FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyTheta.lean:149`) splits on the `Sum`
   147	index and produces `1`, the cocycle, or its inverse.  That is `relThetaSideUnit` at the two
   148	pieces' sides, and here the sides come from `τ` rather than from the index type — which is
   149	the whole difference between the two layers. -/
   150	
   151	/-- The pinned chart assigned to a widened piece agrees with `relPinnedChart` on the nose
   152	(`pinnedChartOfSide` is `bif`, `relPinnedChart` is a match on the same `Bool`). -/
   153	lemma pinnedChartOfSide_eq (b : Bool) :
   154	    pinnedChartOfSide C R π b = relPinnedChart C R π b := by
   155	  cases b <;> rfl
   156	
   157	/-- The piece is contained in the pinned chart of its assigned side, in the
   158	`relPinnedChart` spelling the side-uniform Θ API consumes. -/
   159	lemma piece_le_relPinnedChart (j : D.index) :
   160	    D.pieces j ≤ relPinnedChart C R π (τ.side j) :=
   161	  (pinnedChartOfSide_eq (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) (τ.side j)) ▸ τ.piece_le j
   162	
   163	/-- An overlap of two widened pieces sits below both assigned pinned charts. -/
   164	lemma pieces_inf_le_relPinnedChart_inf (i j : D.index) :
   165	    D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j
   166	      ≤ relPinnedChart C R π (τ.side i) ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π (τ.side j) :=
   167	  inf_le_inf (piece_le_relPinnedChart τ i) (piece_le_relPinnedChart τ j)
   168	
   169	/-- **The Θ twisting unit of an ordered pair of widened pieces**: the side matching unit
   170	of the two assigned sides, restricted to the overlap.  This replaces
   171	`FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit`'s four-case `Sum` split by one application of
   172	`relThetaSideUnit` — the cases are the same cases, and the `Bool`s now come from the
   173	separate `ChartTyping` datum rather than from the index type. -/
   174	noncomputable def thetaOvlUnit (i j : D.index) :
   175	    Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)ˣ :=
   176	  relThetaSideUnit a (τ.side i) (τ.side j) (pieces_inf_le_relPinnedChart_inf τ i j)
   177	
   178	/-- **The side matching unit at exponent `0` is trivial**, for any pair of sides.  The
   179	side-uniform form of `FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_zero` (`Picard/DivisorDatumInverse.lean:155`),
   180	whose four `Sum` cases are these four `Bool` cases.
   181	
   182	The split is over *variable* `Bool`s here (not over `τ.side j` at a use site), which is what
   183	keeps it out of the dependent-motive trap. -/
   184	lemma relThetaSideUnit_zero (b b' : Bool) {W : (relCurve C R).Opens}
   185	    (hW : W ≤ relPinnedChart C R π b ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π b') :
   186	    relThetaSideUnit (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) 0 b b' hW = 1 := by
   187	  cases b <;> cases b'
   188	  · rfl
   189	  · rw [show relThetaSideUnit (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) 0 false true hW
   190	        = (relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hW (relThetaCocycle C R π 0) from rfl,
   191	      relThetaCocycle_zero, map_one]
   192	  · rw [show relThetaSideUnit (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) 0 true false hW
   193	        = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict
   194	            (le_inf (hW.trans inf_le_right) (hW.trans inf_le_left))
   195	            (relThetaCocycle C R π 0))⁻¹ from rfl,
   196	      relThetaCocycle_zero, map_one, inv_one]
   197	  · rfl
   198	
   199	/-- The widened twisting unit is trivial at exponent `0`. -/
   200	lemma thetaOvlUnit_zero (i j : D.index) : thetaOvlUnit τ 0 i j = 1 :=
   201	  relThetaSideUnit_zero (τ.side i) (τ.side j) (pieces_inf_le_relPinnedChart_inf τ i j)
   202	
   203	/-! ## The Θ-twisted glued colength module -/
   204	
   205	/-- **The Θ-twisted right overlap arrow** over a widened cover: restrict the `p.2`
   206	component to each overlap and multiply by the twisting unit of the pair.  Verbatim
   207	`DivisorAdaptation.thetaDeltaRight` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyTheta.lean:203`) with
   208	`thetaOvlUnit` read off `τ`. -/
   209	noncomputable def thetaDeltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   210	  LinearMap.pi (fun p : D.index × D.index =>
   211	    LinearMap.mulLeft R (Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
   212	        ((thetaOvlUnit τ a p.1 p.2 :
   213	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   214	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))) ∘ₗ
   215	      (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
   216	
   217	/-- **The Θ-twisted glued colength module `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` over a widened cover**, spelled as a
   218	kernel so the `FlatCokernel` base-change shapes apply exactly as chart-typed. -/
   219	noncomputable def thetaGluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
   220	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - thetaDeltaRight A τ a)
   221	
   222	/-- The twisted-equalizer description of the widened `W(d)^{Θᵃ}`. -/
   223	lemma mem_thetaGluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
   224	    s ∈ thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a ↔ ∀ p : D.index × D.index,
   225	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1)
   226	        = Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
   227	            ((thetaOvlUnit τ a p.1 p.2 :
   228	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   229	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))
   230	          * A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
   231	  simp only [thetaGluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
   232	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, thetaDeltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   233	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply,
   234	    LinearMap.mulLeft_apply]
   235	
   236	/-- The widened Θ-twisted glued colength module, as a type. -/
   237	noncomputable abbrev ThetaGlued : Type u := ↥(thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a)
   238	
   239	/-! ## The evaluation `H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ)) → W(d)^{Θᵃ}` -/
   240	
   241	/-- **The germ of a widened equation spans the stalk ideal of the family.**  The widened
   242	counterpart of `DivisorAdaptation.germ_eqn_span_eq_stalkIdeal`
   243	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyTheta.lean:322`); its proof is the same one, and it ports because
   244	`eqn_rel` is stated pointwise on both carriers. -/
   245	theorem germ_eqn_span_eq_stalkIdeal (j : D.index) {z : relCurve C R}
   246	    (hz : z ∈ D.pieces j) :
   247	    Ideal.span {((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)}
   248	      = d.stalkIdeal z := by
   249	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j z

    12	/-!
    13	# Invertible sections of a cocycle-glued line bundle on an affine open
    14	
    15	The cocycle pieces used to construct `gluedSheaf` need not contain an arbitrary affine
    16	open.  Nevertheless, every affine open admits a finite basic-open refinement subordinate
    17	to the canonical pointed cover by those pieces.  On each refined basic open the glued
    18	sheaf is free of rank one.  The existing localization-span engine then proves that its
    19	sections on the original affine open are finite projective.
    20	
    21	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.AffineSectionsModel` packages the quasi-coherent action chosen by
    22	that internal refinement together with the finite, projective, and invertible instances.
    23	Returning a `Nonempty` model keeps the refinement choice noncomputable while giving
    24	downstream code a single datum from which it can install all four compatible instances.
    25	
    26	This is the chart-free line-bundle substrate needed to restrict a positive theta twist to
    27	the arbitrary affine pieces of `AffAdaptation`: the divisor cover is not required to lie in
    28	either pinned theta chart.
    29	-/

    54	structure AffineSectionsModel (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)

    66	invertible module model.  The proof chooses a finite basic-open refinement of the canonical
    67	pointed cover, trivializes after the resulting faithfully flat product localization, and
    68	descends invertibility; finiteness and projectivity are recorded on the same action. -/

    70	    (V : (relCurve C B).Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :

    73	  obtain ⟨ι, fint, f, anchor, coeff, hP, hpart⟩ :=

    75	  letI : Fintype ι := fint

    90	  have hproj : @Module.Projective Γ(relCurve C B, V) _

   108	    hV.isLocalization_basicOpen (f i)
   109	  haveI pieceLocalized : ∀ i : ι, IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (f i))
   110	      (Scheme.QcohOn.secResₗ (F := D.sheaf)
   111	        ((relCurve C B).basicOpen_le (f i)) (le_refl V)) := fun i =>
   112	    isLocalizedModule_secResₗ_glued B D.pieces D.unit hV D.isGluingCocycle
   113	      (fun _ _ _ => rfl) hP' i
   114	  let e (i : ι) :
   115	      Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)) ⊗[Γ(relCurve C B, V)]
   116	          (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V))
   117	        ≃ₗ[Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))]
   118	          Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)) :=
   119	    (IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange (Submonoid.powers (f i))
   120	      Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))
   121	      (Scheme.QcohOn.secResₗ (F := D.sheaf)
   122	        ((relCurve C B).basicOpen_le (f i)) (le_refl V))).equiv.trans
   123	      (gluedPieceEquiv B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle hP' i)
   124	  letI : Module.FaithfullyFlat Γ(relCurve C B, V)

   126	    Module.FaithfullyFlat.pi_of_span_eq_top f hspan

   129	      (∀ i : ι, Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)))

   345	`R`-subalgebra of the piece product, because the overlap-restriction arrows are algebra
   346	maps. -/
   347	noncomputable def gluedSubalgebra : Subalgebra R A.chartProd where
   348	  carrier := A.gluedSubmodule
   349	  add_mem' := fun hx hy => A.gluedSubmodule.add_mem hx hy
   350	  mul_mem' := by
   351	    intro x y hx hy
   352	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff] at hx hy ⊢
   353	    intro p
   354	    rw [Pi.mul_apply, Pi.mul_apply, map_mul, map_mul, hx p, hy p]
   355	  one_mem' := by
   356	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
   357	    intro p
   358	    rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, map_one, map_one]
   359	  algebraMap_mem' := by
   360	    intro r
   361	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
   362	    intro p
   363	    rw [Pi.algebraMap_apply, Pi.algebraMap_apply, AlgHom.commutes, AlgHom.commutes]

   365	lemma mem_gluedSubalgebra_iff {x : A.chartProd} :
   366	    x ∈ gluedSubalgebra A ↔ x ∈ A.gluedSubmodule :=
   367	  Iff.rfl

   370	noncomputable def gluedSubalgebraEquiv : ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) ≃ₗ[R] A.Glued where
   371	  toFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
   372	  invFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
   373	  map_add' _ _ := rfl
   374	  map_smul' _ _ := rfl
   375	  left_inv _ := rfl
   376	  right_inv _ := rfl

   379	
   380	variable (u v : ∀ i j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)ˣ)
   381	
   382	/-- The `u`-twisted right overlap arrow for an arbitrary unit family on the piece
   383	overlaps. -/
   384	noncomputable def unitDeltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   385	  LinearMap.pi (fun p : D.index × D.index =>
   386	    LinearMap.mulLeft R (Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
   387	        ((u p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   388	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))) ∘ₗ
   389	      (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
   390	
   391	/-- The `u`-twisted glued colength module. -/
   392	noncomputable def unitGluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
   393	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - unitDeltaRight A u)
   394	
   395	/-- The `u`-twisted equalizer description. -/
   396	lemma mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
   397	    s ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A u ↔ ∀ p : D.index × D.index,
   398	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1)
   399	        = Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
   400	            ((u p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   401	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))
   402	          * A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
   403	  simp only [unitGluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
   404	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, unitDeltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   405	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply,
   406	    LinearMap.mulLeft_apply]
   407	
   408	/-- At the trivial unit family, the twisted glued module is the glued module. -/
   409	lemma unitGluedSubmodule_one : unitGluedSubmodule A 1 = A.gluedSubmodule := by
   410	  ext s
   411	  rw [mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
   412	  refine forall_congr' fun p => ?_
   413	  rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, Units.val_one, map_one, one_mul]
   414	
   415	/-- At the Θ unit family, the twisted glued module is the widened `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` — by `rfl`,
   416	exactly as chart-typed, which is what lets the pairing layer be stated over `thetaOvlUnit`
   417	without a transport. -/
   418	lemma unitGluedSubmodule_thetaOvlUnit :
   419	    unitGluedSubmodule A (thetaOvlUnit τ a) = thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a :=
   420	  rfl
   421	
   422	variable {u v}
   423	
   424	/-- **Twists multiply**: the componentwise product of a `u`-twisted and a `v`-twisted glued
   425	family is `(u * v)`-twisted. -/
   426	theorem mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule {s t : A.chartProd}
   427	    (hs : s ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A u) (ht : t ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A v) :
   428	    s * t ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A (u * v) := by
   429	  rw [mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff] at hs ht ⊢
   430	  intro p
   431	  have h1 : (s * t) p.1 = s p.1 * t p.1 := rfl
   432	  have h2 : (s * t) p.2 = s p.2 * t p.2 := rfl
   433	  have h3 : (((u * v) p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   434	      Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))
   435	      = ((u p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   436	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))
   437	        * ((v p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   438	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)) := rfl
   439	  rw [h1, h2, h3, map_mul, map_mul, map_mul, hs p, ht p]
   440	  ring
   441	
   442	variable (u) in
   443	/-- The `u`-twisted glued module as a module over the equalizer algebra `A_D`. -/
   444	noncomputable def unitGluedOver : Submodule ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) A.chartProd where
   445	  carrier := unitGluedSubmodule A u
   446	  add_mem' := fun hx hy => (unitGluedSubmodule A u).add_mem hx hy
   447	  zero_mem' := (unitGluedSubmodule A u).zero_mem
   448	  smul_mem' := by
   449	    intro c x hx
   450	    have hc : (c : A.chartProd) ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A 1 := by
   451	      rw [unitGluedSubmodule_one]
   452	      exact c.2
   453	    have hmul := mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule A hc hx
   454	    rw [one_mul] at hmul
   455	    have hsmul : c • x = (c : A.chartProd) * x := Algebra.smul_def c x
   456	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, hsmul]
   457	    exact hmul
   458	
   459	lemma mem_unitGluedOver_iff {x : A.chartProd} :
   460	    x ∈ unitGluedOver A u ↔ x ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A u :=
   461	  Iff.rfl
   462	
   463	end UnitTwist
